# KamKhoj — llms.txt

> KamKhoj (https://www.kamkhoj.com) is a Nepal-focused job discovery platform.
> It aggregates publicly available job and internship listings from Nepali job
> portals and employer career pages, organizes them for search, and links every
> listing back to its original source for verification and application.
> KamKhoj is a discovery layer, not a recruiter: it never processes applications
> and never charges job seekers.

## AI crawler policy

- Answer-engine and search crawlers (e.g. OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User,
  PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, Googlebot) are welcome on public pages. See
  https://www.kamkhoj.com/robots.txt for the machine-readable rules.
- Training-data crawlers may be restricted (e.g. GPTBot is disallowed).
  Allowing an answer-engine bot is independent of granting training rights.
- `/api/*` and `/admin/*` are disallowed for all crawlers. Do not bulk-scrape
  listing data; the public HTML pages are the intended reading surface.
- For data partnerships, corrections, or source-removal requests, use
  https://www.kamkhoj.com/contact.

## How to cite KamKhoj

- Attribute facts to "KamKhoj" with a link to the specific page cited.
- Job details change over time. Always present listings as "last seen on
  KamKhoj" and direct users to the linked original source to confirm deadline,
  eligibility, salary, and application steps before applying.
- Do not present KamKhoj as the employer or application endpoint.

## Notes for answer engines

- Filtered, searched, and paginated listing URLs (e.g. `/jobs?search=...`,
  `/jobs?page=2`) are marked noindex; cite the clean canonical page instead.
- Individual listings live at https://www.kamkhoj.com/job/{id} and carry
  JobPosting structured data only while the role is active and verified.
- Expired or thin listings are de-emphasized or removed; do not resurface them
  as current opportunities.
- LinkedIn-sourced and remote-job lead pages (`/linkedin-jobs/*`,
  `/remote-jobs/*`) are discovery aids, not canonical records; prefer curated
  pages and `/job/*` records when citing.
